faq.a1: No. Cards are created in your own bank (Qonto, Revolut Business or Stripe Issuing) and charged to your account. Artemis is software: it applies your rules, collects your approval and drives the bank through its API. It never receives, holds or transfers funds.
faq.q2: What if my agent is manipulated by a prompt injection?
faq.a2: The agent can only ask. Every card is single-use, capped at the exact amount, locked to the intended merchant and expires in 30 minutes. Outside your rules, the request is refused; above your threshold, nothing goes out without your passkey. Any mismatch in amount or merchant triggers an alert, and the “Freeze all” button shuts everything down in one click.
faq.q3: Does the card number go through Artemis?
faq.a3: No, not by default. At checkout, the agent receives a single-use link valid for 10 minutes: the card is displayed there directly by the issuing bank. Artemis never sees, stores or relays the number. Once opened, the link stops working.
faq.q4: Why not just use my bank?
faq.a4: If you only use Stripe, Ramp or Mercury, they already do part of the job. Artemis brings what a bank won't do for its competitors: several banks under a single policy, French accounting (FEC, Pennylane), AI Act proof ready to hand over, and an agency mode.
faq.a5: Stripe Issuing (recommended) creates the cards and displays them to the agent without the number ever going through Artemis. Revolut Business works under a written agreement with Revolut, with the card handed over directly. Qonto connects for reading, freezing and reconciliation. The Sandbox simulates a bank so you can test without connecting anything.
faq.a6: The Sandbox is free. Then {builder} (Builder), {team} (Team), {agency} + {client} per active client ({agencyPlan}) or from {business} (Business) per month. Beyond your quota, {overage} per mandate. No commission on your spending: your bank applies its usual plan. {vat}.
faq.q7: Is my data kept in Europe?
faq.a7: Yes. The database is hosted in the European Union (Frankfurt), bank credentials are encrypted with AES-256-GCM, and the chained audit log documents the human oversight required by the AI Act.
